_comment: Base palette for text-to-world semantic-map generation. Stage 2 (yume-scene-class-catalog) consults this so common terrain + structure classes use the SAME hex across every game — the engine's biome shader (ADR 0055) and extraction script (LLM-as-script-author) can rely on the convention. Per-scene additions (e.g. townhall, market, temple) get new hexes from the EXTENSION palette below, picked to be visually + spectrally distinct from the base. 2026-05-25.

_intent_types.terrain_shader: becomes a biome on the ground shader (ADR 0055). One big plane, not per-pixel objects. Examples: grass, dirt, sand, cobblestone, water surface.
_intent_types.terrain_displacement: drives vertex displacement via heightmap (ADR 0052). Encoded SEPARATELY in the heightmap.png, not in the semantic map's color channel. Examples: hill, valley, river bed.
_intent_types.object_placement: spawned as Yume entities at extracted positions. Examples: house, townhall, well, tree, statue, bridge.

forest.description: Dense tree-covered area (dark green). Use scatter pattern for individual tree entities if walkable forest is needed.

extension_palette.description: saturated yellow — for special anchors (fire pit, brazier, lantern)
saturated purple — for civic/magical structures (temple, shrine, mage tower, storage)
saturated orange — for crafting/work (forge, drying rack, kiln, workshop)
deep red — for important/sacred (townhall, palace, throne room, altar)
teal — for unique features (alchemy, magic pool, healing spring)
mid-saturated green — for farm fields, gardens, orchards
deep brown — for ruined / abandoned structures
cream — for upper-class housing, marble, ceremonial

_authoring_note: Stage 2 of the text-to-world pipeline. The yume-scene-class-catalog skill picks which base classes are present in the scene, plus optionally adds extension-palette classes for scene-specific structures. The skill's OUTPUT format is class_catalog.json with each entry containing {name, hex, intent_type, description, expected_count_or_density}. That catalog drives stages 3 (semantic prompt), 4 (heightmap hints), and 5 (extraction script).
